nodes.name: skill-audit
nodes.description: Audit a third-party skill before adopting it — prompt injection, hidden instructions, unsafe scripts, permission grabs — then judge it against house authoring standards and produce an adoption report. Use when a skill has been pasted, downloaded, copied from a repo or gist, or found online and needs vetting; when asking whether a skill is safe to install; when reviewing a SKILL.md from someone else; or when deciding whether to adopt, revise or reject an incoming skill. Reports only — it never edits the skill.

edges.when: the task needs a component — a toast, drawer, command menu — rather than an animation
critiquing motion that already exists rather than building new motion
auditing a whole codebase for motion problems
hunting for places that could motion-basics
reviewing existing UI rather than diverging on new UI
choosing a dependency rather than building variants
stage 00 — the mechanical scan, before anything is read
the artefact is quarantined and recorded, and judgment begins
edges.note: Referential and not operative by necessity: both are manual-only, so neither can reach the other. That is what keeps the fetch and the reading in separate contexts.

edges.when: nothing is in the inbox yet — there is no other input to this skill
the skill is written, tested, and filed in catalog.json — promotion itself runs promote.mjs directly, never through the Skill tool
edges.note: Referential and not operative, same reasoning as skill-intake → skill-adopt: skill-adopt is manual-only, so no automated flow can reach it.

edges.when: the content came from somewhere else and needs scanning before it is trusted, rather than being written fresh
the bytes came from anywhere else — a URL, a gist, a repo you don't control — so there is provenance to record that an authored skill never has
naming the destination, mapping the frontier, or resolving a Grilling-type ticket
the direction is settled and something has to build from it
edges.note: No such skill is held. The downstream consumer lives outside this library. Declared so the handoff is visible rather than dangling.
